inputs.name: ClaudeCliAdapter.constructor.command
inputs.description: The Claude CLI executable and the leading arguments that come before the adapter's own flags: `discover` runs `command` with `args` plus `--version`, then `auth status --json`, and each turn runs it with `args` plus `-p` and the turn's flags. The default, `claude` with no arguments, applies only when the argument is omitted or undefined, and a failure to start the command surfaces as `reason` from discover or as a rejection from run.

inputs.name: ClaudeCliAdapter.constructor.queue
inputs.description: An optional machine-wide resource queue through which `run` admits each turn under a reservation of 1 CPU and 2048 MiB of memory. When it is omitted, `run` falls back to `resourceWork`, which opens a fresh queue service for that turn, and `discover` never reads it.

inputs.name: ClaudeCliAdapter.run.turn
inputs.description: One Claude CLI turn: `model` is passed as `--model` and the run fails unless the CLI reports that same model, `effort` is passed as `--effort` only when it is a non-empty string, `cwd` becomes the CLI process working directory, and `prompt` is written to its stdin. `access: 'read-only'` adds `--tools Read,Glob,Grep`, while any other value adds no tool limit, and every turn passes `--permission-mode bypassPermissions`; `signal` cancels the run with RunCancelled, and `onText`, `onStatus` and `onFile` receive public CLI text, the 'Waiting for resources' status, and the paths of files Claude writes or edits.

outputs.name: ClaudeCliAdapter.discover
outputs.description: The provider state `discover` resolves to, with `id` 'claude' and `label` 'Claude CLI'. `available` is true, with the single model `claude-opus-5-5`, only when `claude --version` succeeds and `auth status --json` reports `loggedIn` with `authMethod` 'claude.ai'; otherwise `available` is false, `reason` holds the failure message, `version` is set only when the version call succeeded, and `discover` never rejects because every failure is caught into `reason`.

examples.label: Claude CLI
examples.reason: Sign in to Claude CLI with a subscription.

outputs.name: ClaudeCliAdapter.run
outputs.description: The `AgentResult` that `run` resolves to: `text` is the `result` field of the last `result` event (an empty string when absent), and `model` is the model reported by the `system` `init` event. `run` resolves only after the CLI exits with code 0 and its last `result` event is not an error, so `model` always equals `turn.model` in a resolved value.

errors.name: RunCancelled: The run was cancelled.
errors.description: Thrown when the turn's `signal` is aborted: `managedAgentTurn` replaces any error raised after `turn.signal` is aborted with this class, and `cliProcess` throws it when the signal is already aborted or aborts while the CLI runs.

errors.name: ZodError: <schema validation message>
errors.description: Thrown by `resourceRequestSchema.parse` in `resourceWork`, the no-queue path, only when an inherited lease is present and `Number(HARNESS_RESOURCE_CPUS)` is not a positive finite number.

errors.name: Error: Cannot establish resource request owner
errors.description: Thrown by the queue's enqueue step when the identity lookup for this process returns no start time, before the turn is queued.

errors.name: Error: Resource queue is full
errors.description: Thrown by the queue's enqueue step when the queue already holds 512 or more jobs, so the turn is not queued.

errors.name: Error: Invalid inherited resource lease
errors.description: Thrown by the enqueue step only when `HARNESS_RESOURCE_LEASE` is non-empty and names a job that is not running or whose identity check fails.

errors.name: Error: Nested work exceeds its parent resource reservation
errors.description: Thrown by the enqueue step under an inherited lease when the request needs more CPUs or memory than the parent reservation.

errors.name: Error: Resource queue wait timed out; <optional diagnostics>
errors.description: Thrown from the wait loop once the turn has waited more than 1800000 ms (30 minutes), since no `waitTimeoutMs` is passed; the diagnostics (last wait reason, telemetry, CPU and memory figures) are appended only when available.

errors.name: Error: Resource request exceeds usable capacity after reserves
errors.description: Thrown from the wait loop when the resource policy reports the request as impossible for the sampled capacity after reserves.

errors.name: Error: Resource request disappeared
errors.description: Thrown from the wait loop when the scheduled job list no longer contains this turn's job.

errors.name: Error: Parent resource reservation ended
errors.description: Thrown from the wait loop under an inherited lease when the job's parent reservation is no longer running.

errors.name: Error: CLI request timed out.
errors.description: Thrown when the CLI runs longer than the default `timeoutMs` of 600000 ms, since claudeTurn sets none; the CLI process is then sent SIGTERM.

errors.name: Error: CLI output exceeded its limit.
errors.description: Thrown when the CLI's output passes the default `maxBytes` of 16000000 bytes, since claudeTurn sets no limit of its own.

errors.name: Error: <child process error message>
errors.description: Passed through unchanged from the child process's `error` event (for example when the executable cannot be spawned) or from a stdin write error other than EPIPE.

errors.name: Error: CLI failed (<exit code>): <last 2000 characters of stderr>
errors.description: Thrown when the CLI exits with a code other than 0, including `null` after a signal; the message carries that code and the last 2000 characters of stderr.

errors.name: Error: Claude did not run the requested model.
errors.description: Thrown after a successful exit when the model reported by the `system` `init` event differs from `turn.model`, including when no `init` event arrived; no result is returned.

errors.name: Error: <result text reported by Claude, or 'Claude returned no completed result.'>
errors.description: Thrown after a successful exit when no `result` event arrived or the last one has `is_error` set; the message is that event's `result` text when present, otherwise 'Claude returned no completed result.'
